An article from Huntington launches small-biz operating platform “We have a desire to have the most compelling value proposition for small businesses in the country,” Huntington President Brant Standridge said of the bank’s AI-powered 1866 Studio. Published Oct. 19, 2026 Gabrielle Saulsbery Senior Reporter Share Copy link Email LinkedIn X/Twitter Facebook Print License Add us on Google Permission granted by Huntington Bank Huntington Bank is launching an artificial intelligence-powered platform designed to help entrepreneurs manage and grow their small businesses – and it’s not just available to Huntington customers. The 1866 Studio, announced Monday and named after the Columbus, Ohio-based bank’s founding year, aims to simplify workflows for the financial, operational and management needs of a business in one platform powered by Google Gemini. “We have a desire to have the most compelling value proposition for small businesses in the country,” President Brant Standridge said ahead of the launch. “One of the things that we've learned from our 500,000 or so [small-business] customers is that small-business owners wear lots and lots of hats, and there are things that they have to do every day that go far beyond whatever it is that they do in their small business.” With the growing availability of agentic AI technology, Huntington saw the opportunity to use its own technical expertise and technical resources to build agentic tools for its small-business customers. The program aims to relieve business owners of some day-to-day tasks. And 1866 Studio, the bank said, will be capable of providing business launch support, guiding owners through registration and licensing. It will also be able to build marketing strategy, including digital ad copy and social media campaigns. The program will also identify issues the business might run into when seeking financing, the bank said. Powering 1866 Studio initially will be roughly six trained AI agents.
